badge.name: Architect
badge.description: Knows what an agent is made of.

card.title: Agent anatomy
lines: Tools – what it can do (connectors, MCP, APIs)
Harness – the engine between model and agent
Channels – where people use it (Teams, Copilot, web)

steps.title: Every agent has the same building blocks
steps.text: When you open an agent in Copilot Studio you see its building blocks. Tap the numbers to learn what each one does.

callouts.label: Instructions – how the agent should behave, its tone and its limits
Knowledge – the sources it answers from (SharePoint, files, websites…)
Tools – actions it can take (connectors, MCP servers, workflows)
Test pane – chat with your agent before anyone else does
Publish – make the agent available in Teams, Copilot or a website

steps.title: Model + harness = the engine
steps.text:
The **model** does the thinking: it understands the question and writes the answer.

The **harness** is the engine around it. It decides when to call the model, what to send it (instructions, knowledge, tool results), reads what comes back and calls the right tools.

**You** design the agent. The harness and the model do the rest.

steps.question: Put each piece into the right building block.

items.text: Create a repair ticket for a broken espresso machine

steps.explain: **Instructions** shape behavior, **knowledge** is what the agent knows, and **tools** let it take action.

steps.question: Find it! Where would you click to add the HR handbook so the agent can answer from it?
steps.hint: The handbook is something the agent should KNOW.
steps.explain: Use **+ Add knowledge** to connect SharePoint sites, files or websites.

steps.question: A barista asks "How many vacation days do I get?" Put the steps in the right order.
items: The barista asks the question in Teams
The harness and model work out what is needed
The agent searches the HR knowledge source
The model writes an answer from what it found
The answer appears with a citation to the source
steps.explain: Question → plan → search knowledge → generate answer → show it **with a citation** so people can check it.

steps.question: The agent's answer sounds great. How can the barista check where it came from?
options: Trust it – AI is always right
Look at the citation that links to the source
Ask the agent to promise it is correct
steps.explain: Knowledge-based answers can show **citations**. Teach users to click them – it builds trust and catches mistakes.
